stories.title: LG Twins acquire Australian pitcher Jon Kennedy
stories.summary: The LG Twins announced Saturday they have acquired Australian pitcher Jon Kennedy as their new Asian quota player. Kennedy, who signed for US$20,000 for the rest of this Korea Baseball Organization (KBO) season, replaces fellow Australian, Lachlan Wells. Those two were teammates for Australia at this year's World Baseball Classic. Kennedy, 31, has mostly pitched in his native Australia and also has four years of U.S. minor league experience, having reached as high as Triple-A. In the U.S., Kennedy compiled a 10-10 record with a 3.09 ERA over 186 1/3 innings in 94 games. The Twins described Kennedy as a groundball pitcher who will bolster their pitching staff the rest of this season, as they try to win their second straight Korean Series title. Kennedy will be eligible for the postseason if the Twins get there, with Aug. 15 being the annual deadline for KBO clubs to put new foreign players on their active roster to have them available for postseason action. Prior to Saturday's games, the Twins were in third place at 57-47-1 (wins-losses-ties), with the top five teams advancing to the postseason. The Twins were in first place on June 30 but have gone 9-17-1 since July 1, the worst record in the KBO in that span. Wells had a strong start to his 2026 campaign, going 5-2 with a 2.88 ERA in his first 13 starts through June. His season spun out of control in July, though, as he went 0-3 with a 7.20 ERA in five appearances that month. Wells lasted his season-low 2 2/3 innings in his most recent game Aug. 4 and was yanked from the starting rotation.

stories.title: Middle East live: Israel strikes Lebanon in deadliest attack since June
stories.summary: Seven people were killed and at least three injured in an Israeli air strike in southern Lebanon on Saturday, Lebanon's state news ‌agency said. It is the worst toll since deals in June saw a lull in hostilities between Israel and Hezbollah. Follow our live blog for the latest updates.

stories.title: In South Korea, some savour last season of legal dog meat
stories.summary: For decades, the three days of summer considered the hottest of the year were among the busiest for South Korea’s dog meat restaurants, as diners sought traditional stamina-boosting foods to endure the heat. The third “boknal”, or hot day, of 2026 on Friday carried an added sense of finality. It was the last before a nationwide ban on the breeding, slaughter and sale of dogs ‌for meat takes full effect in February 2027. stories.title: Liverpool announce sale of stake in club to Jeff Bezos-backed consortium
stories.summary: On Friday, Liverpool's majority owners Fenway Sports Group announced the sale of a minority stake in the club a consortium including Jeff Bezos and Facebook co-founder Eduardo Savarin. Former Queens Park Rangers owner Amit Bhatia is expected to become the club's new vice-chairman as part of the deal.
